argument:
Sime's positive FY26 profit is established, but its approximately 2.53% headline net-profit/revenue ratio implies a narrow earnings buffer. No matched prior-year revenue comparison or current debt/FCF reconciliation is available. The 9.58x vendor trailing P/E may reflect cyclical earnings assumptions; it is not independently demonstrated undervaluation.

The higher-core-profit headline supports research but does not quantify segment durability or cash returns. Domestic activity can support demand while automobile and industrial cyclicality remain plausible downside channels. Price above both averages is constructive, yet negative MACD histogram and low volume describe consolidation. This is insufficient evidence to buy on headline cheapness; missing leverage detail is uncertainty, not proven distress.
key_points: Low headline earnings margin warrants normalisation.
Low P/E has no matched fair-value support.
Segment cash generation and leverage remain unresolved.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's profitable diversified base is real, but diversification alone does not establish normalised earnings resilience. The higher-core-profit headline and positive price trend cannot fill the missing segment and cash-flow evidence needed to interpret 9.58x earnings.
